title: Evaluation of Evans Blue extravasation as a measure of peripheral inflammation
protocol: Prepare the EB solution for injection in 0.9% saline at a concentration of 50 mg/ml.
Sonicate the prepared EB solution.
Store the sonicated EB solution at 4°C.
Mix 22.6% of Base L-200, 3.7% of Propylene glycol, and 73.7% of distilled water.
Add 1.6% of capsaicin powder to the mixture.
Store the capsaicin cream at room temperature.
Cut aluminium foil into 7-8 cm square pieces and label them with sample numbers.
Prepare Pentobarbital working solution for anesthetizing the rats.
Inject anaesthesia intraperitoneally depending on the weight of the rat (50 mg/Kg).
Wait until the rat is deeply anesthetized.
Cut carefully the vibrissae on both sides of the snout with curved scissors.
Apply depilatory cream to the whisker pad area and leave for 7 or 8 minutes.
Remove the cream with a flat spatula, taking care not to injure or irritate the area.
Rinse the area with gauze wet in distilled water.
Induce vasodilation in the tail vein prior to EB injection.
Immerse the rat tail in warm water to induce vein vasodilation.
Inject the prepared EB solution intravenously in the lateral vein of the tail with an insulin needle at a rate of 0.01 ml/g of animal weight.
Press the injection site with cotton to stop bleeding after removal of the needle.
Refill the syringe and perform subsequent injections more proximally if a lump is formed at the injection site due to broken veins.
Mix capsaicin or vehicle cream according to the group.
Apply the mixture in the whisker pad area on both sides of the snout.
Wait 10 minutes after application and remove the cream using gauze.
Perfuse the animal through the ascending aorta with saline.
Quickly remove the whisker pads.
Dissect the area between the nose and the inferior lip, removing top layers about 5 mm in depth while avoiding intraoral epithelium inclusion.
Wrap each pad separately in aluminum foil, leaving the upper side open for drying.
Place tissue in aluminum foil in an oven at 56°C for two days to dry.
Take the tissue out of the oven after two days and immerse each sample in a plastic tube with formamide, adding 8 ml of formamide per 1 g of dry tissue.
Cover the tubes containing the samples embedded in formamide with aluminum foil.
Leave the plastic tubes containing the samples in an oven at 56°C for two days.
Extract formamide with a pipette after two days in the oven.
Transfer extracted formamide to a covered, labelled eppendorf tube.
Discard the tissue after extracting formamide.
Dilute EB in formamide solution at exponential concentrations of 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 μg/ml.
Prepare dilutions for standard curve just before measuring absorbance.
Take 200 μl of formamide extracted from each sample.
Place 200 μl of each formamide sample in different wells of a P96 multiwell plate.
Add 200 μl of corresponding dilutions for the standard curve to the same plate.
Measure absorbance with a spectrophotometer at a wavelength of 620 nm.
Apply non-linear regression formula to obtain a theoretical standard curve.
Extrapolate the concentration of extravasated EB from the known concentrations of EB and formamide measured in the standard curve.
Normalize all data for comparison across different experimental sessions if measurements were performed on various days.
